remit: underpriced easing, lower-rate repricing, or growth weakness
stance_summary: FACT: CORRA is 2.29 while the tradable 3m CRA 2027H-Z strip implies 3.13/3.365/3.51/3.595, about +84 to +130.5bp from overnight, even as 1m CORRA only reaches 2.58 by Dec-2026. CA labor is 38 with August employment -42k and wages +2.0% y/y, while CPI-trim/median are 1.9%/2.0% and headline is 3.0%. INFERENCE: the 2027 hiking cycle is the energy-pass-through assumption, not the labor/core state, and is the cleanest underpriced-easing discrepancy in the packet. UNKNOWN: whether WTI at 107.02 and BoC minutes force that path anyway. Sidecar is flat. Book OPEN is long-duration the locked CORRA 2027-03/06/09/12 strip, $85m of the $100m cap.

Spot CAD is contaminated by WTI 107.02 (96.4th percentile, +24.23% 1m), a weak USDCAD vs CA-US 2Y link (r-squared 0.022), and CFTC leveraged-fund CAD shorts covering. CA official curve is unavailable so a bond fwd-fwd is blocked. Rates owns the policy-path gap directly.

context_build.causal_mechanism: Restrictive and/or previously eased-but-still-above-neutral Canadian policy is already showing up in the labor channel (employment -42k, wage growth cooling to +2.0% y/y, unemployment 6.4%). Core/trim/median near 2% means the BoC does not need a 2027 hiking cycle unless energy pass-through lifts underlying inflation. If that pass-through fails to enter core, the 2027 CRA strip must reprice lower, not higher.
context_build.path_to_current_price: FACT: overnight CORRA 2.29 as of 2026-09-17. 1m MX contracts: Sep 2.2875, Oct 2.305 (+1.5bp), Nov 2.43 (+14bp), Dec 2.58 (+29bp). 3m CRA then jumps: Sep-26 2.385, Dec-26 2.775 (+48.5bp), Mar-27 3.13 (+84bp), Jun-27 3.365 (+107.5bp), Sep-27 3.51 (+122bp), Dec-27 3.595 (+130.5bp), peaking near 3.655 in 2028. CA 2Y is 3.27 as of 2026-09-17, +31bp 1m, 97.8th percentile 1y, after a -8bp 1d dip. CA 2s10s is 56bp, 0.6th percentile 1y, -18bp 1m, i.e. the front has sold off relative to 10s. This path was built during the post-FOMC global-tightening tape: Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16, SOFR jump to 3.85 on Sep 17, August US CPI keeping a Fed tightening bias, BoC minutes on energy pass-through, WTI +24% 1m, and the desk thesis that the energy shock is constraining easing.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: KNOWN: BoC has already taken CORRA to 2.29, well below SOFR 3.85; energy prices are elevated; Fed just hiked and SR3 still prices more (SR3Z6 4.32, SR3H7 4.58, SR3U7 4.755). NEW enough to explain the 2027 CORRA hike premium: August Canadian employment -42k and wages +2.0% vs +2.8%; August CPI-trim 1.9% and CPI-median 2.0% with headline stuck at 3.0%; Saudi ship-to-ship crude via Oman reducing the extreme oil-supply tail; CA 2Y +31bp over 1m as the global hike narrative was imported into a soft labor market. The 1m strip still only prices +29bp by Dec-2026, so the new information has been loaded into 2027, not the near-term meeting path.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: The tradable 3m CORRA curve requires a delayed but large BoC hiking cycle: roughly +84bp by Mar-2027 and +107 to +130bp through 2027, taking implied CORRA from 2.29 to the mid-3s, on the view that energy pass-through (BoC minutes) and global tightening (Fed/BoJ/BoE split) dominate soft labor and at-target core.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: Disagree that Canada needs ~100bp+ of 2027 hikes. Labor is already contracting and wages are cooling while trim/median sit on 2%. Energy can keep headline at 3% without forcing a reverse of the entire easing cycle. The 1m path through Dec-2026 (+29bp) is closer to a hold-with-option than the 3m 2027 strip.
context_build.price_decomposition: Level: CORRA 2.29 vs 2027 3m implied 3.13-3.595. Change: CA 2Y +31bp 1m / +45bp 3m / -8bp 1d; 2s10s -18bp 1m as 2s led the selloff. Near-term 1m vs 2027 3m is the tenor split: front prices little hiking, 2027 prices a full cycle. Cross-market: CA-US 2Y is -140bp (3.6th percentile), already pricing Canada cheap vs the US in bonds, while Sep-2027 CRA-SR3 is 3.51 vs 4.755 (-124.5bp vs overnight -156bp), i.e. the strip still prices relative Canadian tightening. Marginal driver of the 2027 window is imported energy/Fed-hike beta, not domestic core or labor.

historical_reference.distribution: CA 2Y 3.27 is 97.8th percentile 1y and only 58.5th percentile 5y (z-1y 2.46, z-5y 0.15): rich on a 1y lookback after the +31bp 1m squeeze, not a 5y extreme. CA 2s10s 56bp is 0.6th percentile 1y (z-1y -2.00) after -18bp 1m. CA-US 2Y -140bp is 3.6th percentile (z -1.86). These are discovery screens, not the thesis.
analogs: CA 2Y +31bp 1m analogs: 2022-06-30 (level 3.10) next 1m 0bp / 3m +66bp; 2023-04-14 (3.81) next 1m -1bp / 3m +83bp; 2026-04-01 (2.82) next 1m +12bp / 3m -6bp; 2021-10-14 (0.72) next 1m +28bp / 3m +50bp. CA 10Y +13bp 1m analog 2023-10-23 (4.01) next 1m -36bp / 3m -52bp is the closest easing-repricing episode after an inflation/energy scare. AU housing analog is parallel restriction-biting evidence (NSW stamp duty -24% y/y, transactions -18%, Sydney/Melbourne values >7% off peak) with AONIA still pricing +51bp to Mar-2027 4.86, but AU inflation gauge 82 makes that the worse primary.
historical_reference.regime_differences: 2022-06 and 2023-04 hiking follow-through occurred with high inflation and tighter labor; today CA CPI-trim/median are 1.9%/2.0%, unemployment is 6.4%, employment fell 42k, and wages cooled. 2023-10 yield rally followed a US/global disinflation scare, not a Canadian energy-pass-through debate with WTI at 107. Q2 Canadian GDP +0.8% q/q is a stronger activity backdrop than a classic recession analog. 1m CORRA only extends to Dec-2026 so the policy_paths CA terminal print of 2.58 is a 1m-contract artifact, not the tradable 3m peak.

policy_path_check.rationale: Short-end Canadian trade must use the live CORRA path, not the CA 2Y percentile. The 1m CA terminal of 2.58 is not the tradable 3m peak; paper expression is locked to MX CRA 2027H-Z. US and AU paths are independent checks that CA is pricing more additional hikes than the US despite much weaker labor, and more hiking than Australia's housing-constrained path despite cooler Canadian core.

trade.structure: Locked MX CRA strip average, curve_id CORRA, expiries 2027-03/2027-06/2027-09/2027-12 (CRAH27/CRAM27/CRAU27/CRAZ27). Mark in implied-rate space from tradable_rate_curves; long side is long duration under paper P&L (profits if implied rates fall).
trade.thesis: FACT: overnight CORRA is 2.29 and the 2027 3m strip implies 3.13-3.595 while 1m CORRA is only 2.58 by December; August employment was -42k, wages +2.0% y/y, CPI-trim/median 1.9%/2.0%. INFERENCE: 2027 CRA is pricing an energy-pass-through hiking cycle that domestic labor and core do not require, so receiving that window is the underpriced-easing trade. UNKNOWN: whether WTI 107.02, weaker energy shock-absorbers, and Q2 GDP +0.8% still force BoC to validate the strip. Expression is rates-first; spot USDCAD long is the alternative and is inferior because oil and CAD-short covering can hold CAD up even if CRA 2027 reprices lower.
trade.mispricing: Market prices ~+84 to +130.5bp of CORRA hikes into 2027 versus a 2.29 benchmark, a 38 labor score, contracting employment, and core/trim/median at 2%. The 1m path (+29bp by Dec) does not agree with that 2027 cycle. CA-US 2Y is already -140bp so bond RV is not the residual; the residual is the CRA 2027 hike premium.
why_now: Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% and SOFR 3.85 imported a global tightening beta into CA 2Y (+31bp 1m) and 2027 CRA just as Canadian August labor deteriorated.
BoC minutes flag energy pass-through while Saudi STS workaround and still-at-target trim/median argue that pass-through need not become a hike cycle.
1m CORRA still only +29bp by Dec, so the overpricing is concentrated in the liquid 2027 CRA window the paper book can lock.
Empty sidecar: this is a fresh OPEN, not a duplicate add. Official SOFR vig is 3.85% ACT/360 on the full $100m, so a documented path discrepancy should be funded.

rollup:BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through risk
trade.horizon: 6-10 weeks through Canadian labor and CPI prints and BoC communication; tactical window is the 2027 CRA hike premium, not a multi-year bond rally.
trade.entry: Packet implied-rate mids on tradable_rate_curves.CORRA: CRAH27 3.13, CRAM27 3.365, CRAU27 3.51, CRAZ27 3.595 versus CORRA overnight 2.29 (2026-09-17). Trusted code marks the locked strip average; not a broker quote.
trade.target: Repricing of the 2027 window toward the still-alive near-term path: CRAZ26 2.775 and 1m Dec-2026 2.58 (policy_paths.CA / tradable_rate_curves.CORRA), i.e. fade the 2027 hike cycle rather than a return all the way to 2.29.
trade.invalidation: BoC hikes or explicitly endorses a 2027 path consistent with the CRA strip (mid-3s), or CPI-trim/median leave the 1.9/2.0 area higher while employment stops contracting and wages re-accelerate. A further WTI-driven headline-only spike without core/labor confirmation is not by itself invalidation.
catalysts: Next Canadian employment and wage prints continuing the August contraction/cooling.
Canadian CPI trim/median staying near 2% despite headline 3% and energy.
BoC communications that treat energy as a relative-price shock rather than a 2027 hiking cycle.
Oil-supply tail remaining capped by the Saudi Oman STS workaround.
principal_risks: Energy pass-through from WTI 107.02 and weaker shock-absorbers validates BoC minutes and the 2027 CRA strip.
Q2 GDP +0.8% q/q and activity score 66 mean demand is not collapsing; Ivey PMI was stronger.
Global tightening beta (Fed, BoJ 1.25%, BoE 6-3 hike dissent) keeps term rates bid even if Canadian labor is soft.
